html:
The King's Peace was a peace treaty of 387 BCE that ended the Corinthian War in Greece. Its terms were laid down by the Persian king Artaxerxes II, which is why the Greeks called it the King's Peace. It is also named after Antalcidas, the Spartan envoy who went to the Persian court to arrange it.

The terms were short:

  • The Greek cities of Asia Minor and the island of Cyprus belonged to the Persian king.
  • All other Greek cities, small and great, were to be independent.
  • Whoever refused would face war from the king.

Persian gold had kept the war going, and now Persia settled it. A century after the Greeks beat Xerxes, Persia had won back Ionia without a battle. Sparta became the enforcer of the peace and used the rule of independence to break up rival leagues, such as the Boeotian league led by Thebes. In 382 BCE it even seized the citadel of Thebes. The peace was renewed several times; a quarrel over its renewal in 371 BCE led to the Battle of Leuctra.
